Thursday, November 26

Game recap

WPG4BOS2Final: WPG 4, BOS 2

Winnipeg walked into Boston with Nico Daws in goal and 18 shots in its pocket, and somehow that was plenty. Kyle Connor scored 65 seconds in for his 20th and set up two more, Josh Morrissey made it 2-1 late in the first, and after Morgan Geekie (power play, back on the top unit) and Fraser Minten tied it twice, Morgan Barron put the Jets ahead with 2:07 left in the second. Mark Scheifele hit the empty net with 1:12 to go for a 4-2 final. Daws stopped 21 of 23; Jeremy Swayman saw 17 shots and let in three. Tyrel Bauer and Tanner Jeannot handled the first-period undercard. The Jets are 9-1-1 in their last 11. The Bruins outshot them 23-18 and still lost, which is a pretty good summary of Boston's last 50 springs.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

NYR1BUF5Final: NYR 1, BUF 5

Rasmus Dahlin scored 17 seconds in, and the Rangers spent the next 59 minutes and 43 seconds catching up to the news that the game had started. Josh Norris and Zach Benson scored 33 seconds apart early in the second to make it 3-0, Vladislav Gavrikov got one back with 46 seconds left in the period, and Jack Quinn (his 14th) and Jiri Kulich closed it out in the third, 5-1. Tage Thompson had two assists, and Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen stopped 29 of 30. Joonas Korpisalo, 3-0 as a Ranger coming in, stopped 25 of 30 and took his first loss in blue. Shots were even at 30 apiece; the scoreboard wasn't close. Buffalo is 11-10-4. The Rangers left Buffalo carved up a full day before the turkey.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

CAR3TBL1Final: CAR 3, TBL 1

Carolina doesn't always win pretty. It just wins. Tampa Bay played without Victor Hedman and Erik Cernak (illness) and still led for most of the night on Anthony Cirelli's power-play goal 55 seconds into the second. Then the third period arrived: Eric Robinson tied it unassisted at 5:24, Jaccob Slavin scored his first of the season 97 seconds later, and Jackson Blake hit the empty net with 35 seconds left for a 3-1 final. Brandon Bussi stopped 32 of 33 and Andrei Vasilevskiy 27 of 29. The Hurricanes are the third team in NHL history to win 19 games before Thanksgiving, and their point streak is at eight. Tampa outshot Carolina 33-30 and got one goal for it, which is a lot of Lightning and not much thunder.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

OTT3FLA5Final: OTT 3, FLA 5

Aleksander Barkov and Brad Marchand came back on the same night, and Ottawa's run didn't survive the reunion. Marchand set up Eetu Luostarinen for the opener, then the Senators scored 41 seconds apart early in the second (Dylan Cozens and Philip Tomasino, both from Artem Zub and Jake Sanderson). Niko Mikkola tied it 2-2 with Jacob Markstrom pulled for an extra attacker, Anton Lundell put Florida ahead with 65 seconds left in the second, Sam Bennett scored on the power play, and Barkov's first goal of the season went into the empty net. Michael Amadio's late goal made it 5-3. Marchand finished with three assists. Markstrom stopped 25 of 28; Linus Ullmark gave up four on 31. It's Ottawa's first regulation loss in 10 games. The Senators lead the Atlantic, and Florida just reminded them who's been hanging the banners.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

STL2NYI3SOFinal: STL 2, NYI 3 SO

St. Louis was 2.3 seconds from another win. Then Victor Eklund, with Ilya Sorokin pulled for the extra attacker, tied it 2-2, and the Islanders took the shootout. Jean-Gabriel Pageau opened the scoring in the second, Dylan Holloway answered, and Mason McTavish put the Blues ahead with six minutes left. The Blues played without Jimmy Snuggerud and Pavel Buchnevich and got 27 saves on 29 shots from Joel Hofer; Sorokin stopped 21 of 23. In the shootout, Jake Neighbours scored first, Mathew Barzal answered, McTavish missed, Bo Horvat scored, and Holloway missed to end it. Calum Ritchie had an assist in his return. The Blues played 59:57 of good hockey, then lost the last 2.3 seconds and a skills competition, which is a very St. Louis way to bank one point instead of two.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

CGY6PIT3Final: CGY 6, PIT 3

Pittsburgh scored first, which these days counts as a strong start. Tommy Novak opened it late in the first, and then Calgary scored three in the first 10:37 of the second: Joel Farabee 38 seconds in, then Brennan Othmann and Maxim Tsyplakov with their first goals of the season. Evgeni Malkin's power-play goal moved him past Bryan Trottier into 19th on the NHL's all-time points list, Ryan Strome answered 21 seconds later, and Rickard Rakell scored on the power play 43 seconds after that to make it 4-3. Jonathan Castagna and Yegor Sharangovich (empty net) finished it, 6-3. Dustin Wolf stopped 25 of 28; Arturs Silovs let in five on 26. That's five straight regulation losses for the Penguins, now 7-15-2. Malkin keeps climbing the all-time list, and Pittsburgh keeps sliding down the standings at about the same speed.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

PHI3WSH7Final: PHI 3, WSH 7

Travis Konecny scored 17 seconds in, and the Flyers spent the rest of the night showing why early leads are overrated. Ryan Leonard tied it, Cole Hutson scored on the power play, and Boone Jenner made it 3-1 late in the second. Rasmus Ristolainen pulled Philly within one early in the third, and then the floor gave way: Alex Tuch, Matt Roy into the empty net, Ivan Miroshnichenko and Dylan Strome, four Washington goals in 2:48, with Cole Knuble's goal squeezed in between. Tuch had a goal and two assists. Logan Thompson stopped 18 of 21; Joseph Woll gave up six on 34. The Capitals ended a five-game losing streak and outshot Philadelphia 35-21. Rick Tocchet called it embarrassing and said his team gave in. The Flyers came to D.C. for Thanksgiving and handed out seven.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

NJD3CBJ2SOFinal: NJD 3, CBJ 2 SO

New Jersey needed a shootout to beat Columbus, and Columbus needed someone, anyone, to score in it. Nico Hischier opened the scoring, Cole Sillinger tied it, and Evan Rodrigues put the Devils back ahead on the power play with 37 seconds left in the second. Luca Del Bel Belluz scored his first of the season to tie it 2-2 at 8:48 of the third, and nobody scored again until Arseny Gritsyuk, the only shooter to beat a goalie in the shootout. Connor Hellebuyck stopped 22 of 24, then Charlie Coyle, Valeri Nichushkin and Kent Johnson. Cam Talbot made 24 saves on 26. Jesper Bratt passed Scott Niedermayer for second on the Devils' career assists list. Brenden Dillon was ejected for an illegal check to the head of Denton Mateychuk and has a Player Safety hearing today. Columbus went 0 for 3 in the shootout and is 9-13-1, so at least it's consistent.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

VAN1DET5Final: VAN 1, DET 5

Vancouver's four-game road trip opened with Emmitt Finnie scoring twice in the first 4:05, which is a rough way to unpack a suitcase. Lucas Raymond added a power-play goal late in the first, J.T. Compher made it 4-0 in the second, and Viktor Arvidsson finished with a goal and two assists. Paul Cotter scored for the Canucks midway through the third, and Arvidsson answered 42 seconds later for the 5-1 final. Daniil Tarasov stopped 25 of 26; Leevi Meriläinen gave up five on 26. Kirby Dach was plus-1 in his Detroit debut, and Cole Reinhardt had six hits in his first game as a Canuck. Vancouver is 6-20-1 with 13 points in 27 games, which would put the Canucks in the draft lottery conversation if they weren't already leading it.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

NSH3DAL1Final: NSH 3, DAL 1

Mavrik Bourque went 21 games without a goal this season and saved the first one for his old team. He scored with 58 seconds left in the first, and then Juuse Saros and Jake Oettinger turned it into a goalie duel: nobody scored again until the final 81 seconds. Ross Colton hit the empty net, Wyatt Johnston answered with Oettinger pulled, and Jack Drury added another empty-netter with 15 seconds left for a 3-1 final. Saros stopped 20 of 21; Oettinger stopped 24 of 25 and lost anyway, the goaltending version of pitching a gem and losing 1-0. Tyler Myers was back for Dallas after three games out. Nashville ended the Stars' five-game win streak. Dallas had won its last four by one goal apiece, and the bill for living that close to the edge finally came due.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

UTA4MIN3Final: UTA 4, MIN 3

Minnesota hadn't lost in regulation in 15 games. Utah, with 20 shots, took care of that. Lawson Crouse scored early, Logan Cooley got his 13th on the power play, and the second period turned into a brawl with a scoreboard: Jack McBain fought Michael McCarron 27 seconds in, Liam O'Brien took on Nick Foligno at 3:14, and the teams traded four goals. Dmitri Simashev and Dylan Guenther scored for Utah, Bobby Brink (unassisted, on the power play) and Blake Coleman for the Wild. Coleman scored again with 4:04 left, but Karel Vejmelka held on with 22 saves on 25. Jesper Wallstedt let in four on 20. Kirill Kaprizov's 15-game point streak ended with the Wild's run. Minnesota is still 18-4-5, but losing to a team that shot 20 times is the kind of thing that makes a Wild fan check the playoff history again.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

MTL0COL6Final: MTL 0, COL 6

Cale Makar came back, and the Avalanche celebrated by making Montreal disappear. Logan O'Connor scored for the first time since March 31, 2025, Artturi Lehkonen got his 16th 30 seconds into the second, and Devon Toews scored twice late in the period, the second with six seconds left, for a 4-0 lead. Martin Necas had a goal and two assists, Gabriel Landeskog added a power-play goal, and Makar finished with three assists. Mackenzie Blackwood stopped all 28 shots, and Colorado is the first team with three straight home shutout wins since the 2016-17 Blue Jackets. Jacob Fowler faced 38 shots and saw six go in. Montreal paid two first-round picks for Dylan Larkin, and on this night it got 28 shots and a 6-0 bill for the trip to Denver.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

CHI3SEA1Final: CHI 3, SEA 1

Forty minutes of nothing, and then Chicago won its third straight road game. Cole Smith broke the scoreless tie at 5:58 of the third, Roman Kantserov scored on the power play 94 seconds later, and after Jordan Eberle got one back with Joey Daccord pulled, Kantserov hit the empty net from 154 feet for a 3-1 final. Spencer Knight stopped 29 of 30; Daccord stopped 16 of 18. The Blackhawks won with 19 shots, swept their three-game trip and went from 0-8-1 on the road to 3-8-1 in five days. Seattle outshot Chicago 30-19 at home and lost, and if you can't beat the Blackhawks on 19 shots, the Kraken's Thanksgiving menu is mostly crow.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

SJS0ANA7Final: SJS 0, ANA 7

The Sharks had nothing left to be thankful for by the middle of the first period. Anaheim scored three times in 1:40 (Judd Caulfield, Alex Killorn, and Cutter Gauthier on the power play), then Ian Moore, Roger McQueen, Frank Vatrano and Killorn again made it 7-0. Laurent Brossoit, called up the same day, stopped all 22 shots for his first shutout since April 11, 2024. Mikael Granlund had three assists. Gauthier's goal was his 23rd of the season and his 19th in November, one short of the NHL record of 20 in a month, with two November games left. Alex Nedeljkovic played all 60 minutes and let in seven on 30. San Jose's rebuild has plenty of nights like this one left in it; this one just came with seven receipts.

Wednesday, November 25

Game recap

VGK5EDM3Final: VGK 5, EDM 3

The Oilers came home to stop the bleeding and needed all of six minutes to reopen it. Jack Eichel scored on the power play at 6:13, Trevor Connelly made it 2-0 unassisted three minutes later, and Edmonton spent the second period climbing back: Colton Dach at 3:03, then Connor McDavid's 14th with 19 seconds left to tie it. The reward for all that work was Nic Dowd, who picked 2:08 of the third for his first goal of the season. Eichel got his second at 5:29, Vasily Podkolzin answered 16 seconds later with his 14th, and Connelly's empty-netter gave him two goals and an assist. Carter Hart made 21 saves on 24 shots, Devon Levi 22 on 26. Vegas is 15-6-5 and three points back of first with a game in hand. Edmonton has dropped four straight after a 17-3-3 start. The Oilers usually wait until June to let everybody down; this year they're getting it done before Thanksgiving.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Each game is scored for an average team in that team's shoes: the opponent's strength (its record this season, blended with our power rankings, plus a little recent form), home or away, rest (back-to-backs, extra days off) and travel (time zones crossed, how deep into a road trip). Scores are graded against the whole league: 0 is an average game, +5 is among the easiest ~1% of games anyone plays this season, −5 among the hardest. Rest of season shows every game still to play, Next 5 the next five, and Last 15 / 10 / 5 the final 15, 10 or 5 games of each team's season (the stretch run). Played games are faded in the game-by-game view.
